criteria.text: Identifies that the board approval was given at a meeting with only 2 directors present when Article 11 requires a quorum of three, so the approval may be invalid, and recommends a fresh or ratifying resolution.

Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 45-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.
Calculates the long-stop date as 30 July 2027 (150 days after signing on 2 March 2027) and identifies that expected clearance on 13 September 2027 falls after it, recommending an extension.
Identifies that the basket in SPA Section 9.4 ($1,850,000) operates as a deductible (Seller liable only for the excess), not a tipping basket, and explains that this is less favourable to the Buyer.
Gives the long-stop period as 150 days and as the date 30 July 2027, with days remaining from 18 March 2027 (134 days).
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
Checks whether computed deadlines fall on a weekend and adjusts them under the documents' Business Day definition.
